_doc: Regulatory questions job aid: six rows. The rep reads the row's line out loud as written, does not paraphrase and does not improvise. `escalation_criteria` says when the row is not enough and the question goes to compliance. Point-of-use support (Rossett & Schafer, 2007): the objective is performance with the aid, not memorisation.

rows.what_it_means: Know Your Customer, the identity checks at signup
rows.rep_response_verbatim: We run KYC at signup, and it takes the owner about 10 minutes. The process is smoother than your bank's.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the buyer asks about the list of accepted documents, beneficial-ownership thresholds, KYC rules in a particular country or how we handle politically exposed persons (PEPs).

rows.what_it_means: Anti-Money Laundering, the monitoring of transactions
rows.rep_response_verbatim: Every transaction is monitored. You will not see this as a customer unless something gets flagged, which is rare and we walk you through it.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the buyer asks about our transaction-monitoring rules, how many suspicious activity reports we file, false-positive rates or how a flag would show up in their accounting.

rows.what_it_means: Strong Customer Authentication, the approval of payments with two factors
rows.rep_response_verbatim: Card payments in the EU need Strong Customer Authentication unless an exemption applies. Your cardholder approves with a push on their phone, and it takes a couple of seconds. Which payments count as exempt is a question for our compliance team.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the buyer asks about SCA delegation, how exemptions are decided (low-value, trusted-beneficiary or transaction-risk) or merchant-side SCA flows in a particular country.

rows.what_it_means: Payment Services Directive, the EU rules for payment services and open banking
rows.rep_response_verbatim: We work under PSD2, the EU rules for payment services. Among other things, it's what lets a licensed provider like us work alongside your existing bank instead of replacing it. Anything more specific, I'll bring in our compliance team.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate on any PSD2 follow-up question, such as open-banking consent, third-party provider (TPP) registration, AISP or PISP licensing, the RTS on SCA or cross-border passporting. Sales only uses the PSD2 line as a reference.

rows.what_it_means: EU data protection, covering where your data is stored and what we do with it
rows.rep_response_verbatim: Your card data is stored in the EU. We don't sell it, and we only share it with the payment partners needed to process your transactions, as our DPA sets out. Happy to send the DPA over.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the buyer asks about transfers outside the EU (SCCs, or adequacy for Switzerland, the UK or the US), our sub-processors, deadlines for data requests from former employees or audit clauses in the DPA.

rows.what_it_means: the protection of customer money if we fail
rows.rep_response_verbatim: Your money sits in a separate safeguarded account at a tier-1 bank, apart from our own funds. If we ever failed, it's ring-fenced for customers and can't be used to pay our creditors.
rows.escalation_criteria: Escalate if the buyer asks which bank holds the funds, how long a return would take, how insolvency would work or how safeguarding compares with deposit insurance.

honest_carve_out.principle: When the buyer goes deeper than a row, book the compliance team.
